definitions_and_laws.definition: differentiate between physical and non-physical quantities;
exemplify that physics is based on physical quantities only;
identify various physical quantities as base and derive quantities;
list the seven base quantities of International System (SI) along with their symbols and units;
differentiate between base and derived physical quantities and units;
convert prefixes and their symbols to indicate multiples and sub-multiples for base and derived units;
convert numerical values of measurement in scientific notation;
differentiate between scalar and vector quantities;
list out various physical quantities as scalar or vector;
describe the ‘head to tail’ rule of vector addition;
determine, using Pythagoras theorem and graphs, the resultant of two vectors at right angle;
determine the least count (LC) of the measuring instruments;
describe the working of measuring instruments;
determine an average value of the measurement by measuring multiples values of the quantity;
identify sources of errors (systematic and random) in the measurement;
apply the rules for rounding a number to the appropriate number of significant figures.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the volume of one cube is $1.76\text{ cm}^3$, then the volume of twenty-one such cubes rounded off to three significant figures is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Total volume = 21 * 1.76 = 36.96 cm³. When rounded off to 3 significant figures, 36.96 becomes 37.0 cm³.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The number 123.4 can also be written in scientific notation as
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: To express 123.4 in standard scientific notation ($a \times 10^n$ where $1 \le |a| < 10$), the decimal point is moved two places to the left, giving $1.234 \times 10^2$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The prefix used for the multiple value of $10^{-9}$ is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The SI prefix for $10^{-9}$ is nano.
